STUDENT RESEARCH AND INNOVATION PROGRAM Description One of the core commitments of the University of Cabuyao is to create, apply, and communicate research-based knowledge that is significant to industry and society.
At the heart of this commitment is a focus on prioritizing and emphasizing the importance of research in the educational experience of the student.
The University recognizes that research provides a unique opportunity for students to develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and analytical skills, while also fostering a deeper understanding of the subject matter.
To ensure that research conducted by students meets the highest standards of quality, the University measures the quality of research by several different criteria.
These criteria include the format of the research paper or project, the logical presentation of the research findings, the theoretical foundation upon which the research is based, the consistency and coherence of the research arguments, the quality of language development, and the credibility and reliability of the sources cited in the research.
By setting high standards for research quality, the University seeks to foster a culture of excellence in research among its students and faculty.
This not only benefits the institution but also contributes to the wider societal goal of advancing knowledge and innovation.
The University encourages and supports innovation and start-up projects among students, teaching, and non-teaching personnel of the University.
The guideline aims to create a conducive environment for the development of entrepreneurial skills and the commercialization of intellectual property.
The University intends to foster a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship among its students, teaching, and non-teaching personnel.

By providing necessary support and resources, the University seeks to unleash the potential of young innovators and create a vibrant start-up ecosystem that can drive economic growth and development.

MESSAGE FROM THE CITY MAYOR/ CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD Mahal naming mga mananaliksik, mga tagapayo, mga panel, at mga coordinator ng pananaliksik, Pinapaabot namin ang pinakamainit na pagbati at taos-pusong pasasalamat sa inyong mahahalagang kontribusyon sa larangan ng pananaliksik at pag-aaral.
Sa patuloy na pagbabago ng larangan ng akademya at pagtuklas, ang pananaliksik ay may malaking papel sa pagpapaunlad, paghubog ng mga patakaran, at pagharap sa mga hamon ng ating panahon.
Ang inyong kolektibong pagsisikap at intelektuwal na pagkilos ay may kakayahan na mag-anyo ng kinabukasan at transpormahin ang ating komunidad.
Sa pamamagitan ng mahigpit na mga metodolohiya, malawakang pagsusuri sa mga panitikan, at matalinong pagsusuri ng datos, inyong ibinibigay ang liwanag sa mga komplikadong isyu, nagpapakita ng mga bagong perspektibo, at nag-aambag sa pandaigdigang kaalaman.
Isa-isa, bilang isang kolektibong puwersa, ipinagdiriwang natin ang inyong paghahangad sa kaalaman, pagbabago, at intelektuwal na paglago.
Ang inyong pananaliksik ay nagiging tanglaw ng pag-asa, patungo sa mga solusyong batay sa ebidensya, nagtataguyod ng pangmatagalang kaunlaran, at nagpapayaman sa ating kolektibong pagkaunawa sa mundo na ating kinabibilangan.
Nawa'y maglingkod ang Student Research and Innovation Manual na ito bilang inyong pinagkakatiwalaang gabay, nag-aalok ng kaalaman, etikal na gabay, at mga pinakamahusay na pamamaraan na magtutulak sa inyo patungo sa inyong paglalakbay sa pananaliksik.
Sabay-sabay, ating itulak ang mga hangganan, lumikha ng kinabukasang itinayo sa kaalaman, pagbabago, at transformatibong pananaliksik.
HON.
DENNIS FELIPE C.
HAIN (Sgd) City Mayor/Chairman of the Board

10.
Patent Search for Engineering.
Performing a patent research on student researches involves searching for existing patents or published patent applications related to the students' research topics.
By following the following steps, the students can gain valuable insights into the existing patent landscape related to their research and make informed decisions about the patentability and commercialization potential of their inventions. a.
Define the Research Topic: Clearly identify the specific research topic or invention concept that the student is working on.
Understand the unique features and technical aspects of the project to use relevant keywords during the search. b.
Keyword Search: Conduct a keyword search using online patent databases and search engines.
Use specific and relevant keywords related to the research topic to narrow down the search results. c.
Use Patent Classification: Utilize patent classification systems such as the International Patent Classification (IPC) or Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) to categorize and filter patents related to the research area. d.
Prior Art Search: Look for prior art, which includes existing patents, published patent applications, and other publicly available technical documents relevant to the research topic.
Prior art helps determine the novelty and non-obviousness of the student's invention. e.
Search Multiple Databases: Utilize various patent databases and search engines, such as the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), European Patent Office (EPO), World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), and Google Patents, to ensure comprehensive coverage of relevant patents. f.

section_path: GUIDELINES > CHAPTER I STUDENT TERMINAL PROGRAM > Section 2. Specific Policies
text:
GUIDELINES > CHAPTER I STUDENT TERMINAL PROGRAM > Section 2. Specific Policies
Analyze Patent Documents: Carefully review the patent documents found during the search.
Pay close attention to the patent claims, which define the scope of protection granted to the invention.
Compare the students' research with the patented inventions to assess the novelty and potential patentability.

section_path: GUIDELINES > CHAPTER I STUDENT TERMINAL PROGRAM > Section 2. Specific Policies
text:
GUIDELINES > CHAPTER I STUDENT TERMINAL PROGRAM > Section 2. Specific Policies
g.
Note Similarities and Differences: Identify any patents that are closely related to the students' research and note the similarities and differences between their work and the patented inventions.
This will help the students understand the existing technology landscape and potential areas for improvement or differentiation. h.
Seek Legal Assistance: If the students' research shows potential for patentability, it is advisable to seek advice from the Director for Knowledge Management and Innovation Department.
S/he can help determine whether the invention meets the patentability criteria and guide the students through the patent application process. i.
Document the Search Process: Keep detailed records of the search process, including search terms used, databases accessed, and search results.
This documentation will be valuable for future reference and to demonstrate due diligence in conducting the patent research.

On Acknowledgment and Dedication i.
Research should be written in clear and concise language that is accessible to a wide audience.
Researchers are expected to avoid jargon, slang, and colloquialisms that may be difficult for non-experts to understand.
The use of non-standard English or local languages may be permitted in certain circumstances, but must be approved by the supervisor or department head. ii.

The research text should be written in the third-person orientation d.

The summary shows the history, highlights, descriptive definitions, long-range objectives, feasibility criteria for FS, and main conclusions of the project under study. ii.

CHAPTER II INSTITUTIONAL AND STUDENT RESEARCH ETHICS REVIEW PNC:PRE-GU-13 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
It is the responsibility of all researchers to adhere to the principles and procedures outlined in this guideline to ensure that research activities are conducted in an ethical and responsible manner.
2.
All research proposals involving humans as participants/subjects shall be submitted to RERC for ethics review and clearance.
This follows various international and national guidelines that have been developed for the protection of human participants in research.
3.
All researchers must include a description that outlines the ethical considerations of their studies in protocols/methodologies.
4.
Research Ethics Review Committee (RERC) a.
The committee shall govern the ethics of research across the University.
It ensures the dignity, protection of rights, health and safety and privacy of human subjects, the welfare of animals, and the integrity of the environment.
It also upholds the academic freedom, health, and safety of researchers and the reputation of the University as an institution of high-quality research. b.
The RERC comprises seven members with various educational backgrounds.
A legal representative shall be invited to serve as a regular member of the committee.
Further, an independent consultant shall be invited to guide the RERC, as needed.

c.
The scope of work of the RERC covers all researches involving human participants for completion of an undergraduate thesis, graduate research, faculty researches as well as researches referred by other institutions such as HEIs, government agencies, among others. d.
The creation of the Research Ethics Review Committee (RERC) is in compliance with the guidelines set forth by the Philippine National Health Research System (PNHRS), specifically the Philippine Health Research Ethics Board (PHREB); the DOST, DOH, CHED, UPM Joint Memorandum Order 2012-001, which outlines the requirements for ethical review of health research involving human participants; and the DOST-PCHRD, DOH, CHED, UPM-NIH Administrative Order 001-2013, which serves as the implementing rules and regulations of RA 10532, or the Philippine National Health Research System Act of 2013. e.
In accordance with the University's commitment to upholding the highest ethical standards in research, the RERC operates independently of other offices, units, and administrative officials in the university.
This independence is essential to ensuring that the review and decision-making process of the RERC is objective, impartial, and free from any external influence. f.
Therefore, the decisions of the RERC with respect to its reviews of research protocols are not subject to the influence, regulation, or approval of any other office or official in the institution.
The RERC operates with complete autonomy and makes decisions based solely on the merits of the research proposals that come before it, without any undue influence from external sources. g.

All researchers should adhere to the following principles: a.
Respect for Human Dignity.
All research activities must respect all human beings' inherent dignity and worth. b.
Informed Consent.
Informed consent (PNC:PRE-FO-50) must be obtained from all research participants before conducting any research activities.
All research participants must be provided with clear and understandable information about the research project, including any potential risks and benefits associated with participation.
Informed consent must be obtained from all research participants prior to their participation in the research project.
Parental consent form (PNC:PRE-FO-51) shall be accomplished for research participants who are below 18 years old. c.
Privacy and Confidentiality.
All research activities must respect the privacy and confidentiality of research participants.
Researchers must take all necessary steps to protect the privacy and confidentiality of research participants. d.
Responsibility for Safety.
All researchers have a responsibility to ensure that the research activities are conducted safely and responsibly.

Integrity and Accountability.
All research activities must be conducted with the highest levels of integrity and accountability.
Researchers must ensure that the research is conducted in a transparent and responsible manner, and that all data collected is accurate and verifiable.
3.
Confidentiality Agreement Form (PNC:PRE-FO-47) and Disclosure of Conflict of Interest Form PNC:PRE-FO-48) a.
The members of the RERC play a crucial role in ensuring that research studies conducted at the institution are ethical and comply with all relevant guidelines and regulations.
To ensure the integrity of the review process, it is essential that all members of the RERC maintain strict confidentiality and disclose any potential conflicts of interest. b.
To this end, all members of the RERC are required to sign a Confidentiality Agreement Form (PNC:PRE-FO-47) and a Disclosure of Conflict of Interest Form (PNC:PRE-FO-48). c.
The Confidentiality Agreement Form outlines the obligations of RERC members to maintain strict confidentiality with respect to all research proposals and related documents that come before the committee.
This includes not disclosing any information related to the proposals to any unauthorized third party or using such information for personal gain or advantage. d.
The Disclosure of Conflict of Interest Form requires all RERC members to disclose any potential conflicts of interest that could impact their ability to review research proposals objectively and impartially.
This includes financial interests, personal relationships, or any other factors that could influence their decision-making. e.

4.
Research Ethics Review a.
Exempted Review i.
Research projects that involve the collection of data from publicly available databases or public documents are exempt from review. ii.
This exemption recognizes that the collection of data from public sources is generally considered to pose minimal risk to research participants, and as such, does not require the same level of review and scrutiny as other research activities. b.
Expedited Review i.
Expedited Review is used for research proposals that are deemed to have lower complexity and minimal risk.
These are typically studies that involve standard research procedures and pose minimal harm to participants. ii.
Expedited review shall be conducted for the following:
• Research projects that pose minimal risk to participants and involve standard, non-invasive procedures are prime candidates for expedited review.
These studies do not expose participants to risks greater than what they might encounter in their daily lives or routine medical check-ups.
• Research that consists of anonymous or de-identified surveys, questionnaires, or interviews may qualify for expedited review, especially when the questions are not sensitive in nature and the risks are minimal.

CHAPTER V INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS PNC:PRE-GU-18 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The Knowledge Management and Innovation Department (KMID) shall be the coordinating office of the University with Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines (IPO-PHL) on applying for intellectual property-related matters of institutional and student researches in the University 2.
KMID shall spearhead the promotion of utilization and technology transfer of research outcomes within the University and to prospective industry companies.
3.
The University shall own the intellectual property rights created by teaching and non-teaching personnel as part of his/her duties and those created by students under the conditions stated in the succeeding section.
4.
Research outcomes with potential intellectual property value presented in public either by colloquium, symposium, conference, or exhibit shall only be given 10 months to apply for the outcome for protection with IPO-PHL from the date of presentation.
Otherwise, these will lose their novelty and will no longer qualify for registration.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
On IP Creation a.
Innovation is embedded in the University's mission, and it is dedicated to fostering a culture of creativity.
With the implementation of InnovateUC, the University aims to elevate academic experiences and propel the institution into a
hub of groundbreaking ideas.
Recognizing the importance of intellectual property, the University will encourage the creation, protection, and commercialization of novel concepts. b.

The KMID shall secure intellectual property protection to facilitate the commercialization of works, trademarks, innovations, inventions, and safeguard scientifically significant discoveries. c.

In line with UC PnC commitment to promoting a culture of transparency, collaboration, and responsible intellectual property management, all IP Creators are required to disclose their developments to the University, using the prescribed form (PnC:PRE-FO-99). e. f.
Within one month of receiving the IP Disclosure form, KMID shall communicate in writing to the IP creator, confirming whether the University intends to pursue the registration and/ or commercialization of the IP, taking into consideration any obligations to external parties. g.
The IP creator is obligated to maintain the confidentiality of technology details while the University assesses the feasibility of commercialization and/or registration.
Any form of publication, including verbal disclosure, describing a plant, invention, innovation, or discovery before patent filing could jeopardize the registration process. h.
Throughout the evaluation, the IP creator must refrain from public disclosure until the appropriate IP application has been filed.
University is committed to minimizing delays in the application process.

IP Creators should be vigilant to prevent prejudicial disclosure that could harm

This includes avoiding disclosures that might negatively impact patentability or other forms of protection. b.

Confidential Information.
All parties involved in intellectual property-related activities must treat confidential information with the utmost care.

Individuals privy to confidential information are legally obligated not to disclose such information to unauthorized parties.

Limited disclosure of confidential information may occur in collaborative endeavors.

The University of Cabuyao encourages the identification and documentation of trade secrets within the institution.
This includes confidential formulas, processes, techniques, or information providing a competitive advantage. ii.

Robust protection mechanisms should be implemented to safeguard trade secrets, including restricted access, encryption, and contractual agreements.

General Statement on Obligations, Conflict of Interest, and Conflict of Commitment in the Intellectual Property Policy of the University of Cabuyao a.
General Obligations.
All individuals engaged in research, innovation, and intellectual property activities at the University of Cabuyao are obligated to adhere to ethical standards, transparency, and accountability.
This includes a commitment to honest and accurate reporting, responsible use of resources, and compliance with relevant laws and regulations governing intellectual property. b.
Conflict of Interest.
To maintain the integrity of the intellectual property process, individuals must disclose any potential or actual conflicts of interest that may compromise the unbiased and fair evaluation of IP matters.
Such conflicts could arise from personal, financial, or professional interests that may influence decision-making related to intellectual property ownership, protection, and commercialization. c.
Conflict of Commitment.
Individuals associated with the university must manage conflicts of commitment that may arise from simultaneous professional obligations outside the university.
Balancing external commitments with responsibilities to the University of Cabuyao is essential to ensure that intellectual property matters receive the necessary attention and dedication.
9.
Dispute Resolution.
In the event of disputes related to IP ownership, protection, or commercialization, the following dispute resolution process will be followed: a.

Parties involved in the dispute are encouraged to engage in open communication and seek an informal resolution. ii.

or department heads to address concerns and explore mutually agreeable solutions. b.
Mediation i.
If an informal resolution is not achieved, the parties may opt for mediation facilitated by a neutral third party. ii.
The mediator will work with the involved parties to explore options, clarify issues, and guide discussions toward a resolution. iii.
Mediation is voluntary, confidential, and aims to preserve relationships while addressing the core issues of the dispute. c.
Dispute Resolution Committee i.
If mediation does not result in a resolution, the matter may be referred to a Dispute Resolution Committee constituted by the University. ii.
The Committee will comprise individuals with expertise in relevant fields, including legal, academic, and administrative representatives. iii.

Arbitration i.
In cases where resolution is not achieved through the Dispute Resolution Committee, parties may choose to engage in arbitration. ii.
Arbitration is a formal process where an impartial arbitrator or panel hears the case, reviews evidence, and issues a binding decision. iii.
The decision of the arbitrator is final and enforceable, providing a structured mechanism for resolving disputes.

CHAPTER VI MANAGEMENT OF INNOVATION AND START-UP PROJECTS PNC:PRE-GU-20 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The University, through the Knowledge Management and Innovation Department, shall create a supportive environment for innovation and start-up projects, by providing necessary resources, facilities, and mentoring support to students and teaching and non-teaching personnel.
2.
The University shall encourage and incentivize students and teaching and non-teaching personnel to participate in innovation and start-up projects, by offering grants, seed funding, and other financial and non-financial support through partnership with government or private agencies.
3.
The University shall establish mechanisms to protect and commercialize intellectual property arising from innovation and start-up projects, by providing legal and technical support to students and teaching and non-teaching personnel.
4.
The University shall collaborate with industry partners and investors to facilitate the commercialization of innovation and start-up projects, by providing networking and matchmaking opportunities to students and faculty members.
5.
The University shall ensure that innovation and start-up projects are aligned with its philosophy and objectives, and that they adhere to ethical and legal standards Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
Students, teaching, or non-teaching personnel who intend to venture into start-up projects shall submit the Innovation and Start-
up Project Form (PNC:PRE-FO-56) to KMID.
2.

3.

KMID shall organized an Innovation Technical Committee (ITC) who shall guide the innovators-applicants.
It is a a group of experts who are responsible for reviewing and evaluating innovation-related projects and initiatives within an organization.
The committee is typically composed of three individuals with specialized knowledge and experience in innovation, technology, research and development, and related fields.
4.
Following are the roles of the ITC: a.
Evaluate new ideas and proposals: The committee reviews and evaluates new ideas and proposals submitted by individuals or teams within the organization.
They assess the feasibility, potential impact, and technical aspects of the proposals and provide recommendations for further development or implementation. b.
Develop innovation strategies: The committee works with the University to develop innovation strategies that align with the University's philosophy and objectives.
They identify areas of opportunity, potential risks, and help set priorities for innovation projects. c.
Provide technical expertise: The committee provides technical expertise and guidance to project teams, helping them to overcome technical challenges and identify solutions to complex problems. d.
Monitor progress: The committee monitors the progress of ongoing innovation projects, tracks key performance indicators, and provides feedback to project teams to ensure that they stay on track and achieve their goals.

e.
Foster a culture of innovation: The committee helps to foster a culture of innovation within the University by encouraging and supporting individuals and teams to think creatively and develop new ideas and solutions.
5.
Following are the processes to be observed. a.
Ideation i.
KMID shall create venues for ideation.
This involves generating and refining ideas for a new product, service, or technology.
The goal is to identify a gap in the market or a specific problem that needs to be solved. ii.
During the ideation process, it is important to identify and gather relevant knowledge about the problem or opportunity.
This can include both internal knowledge (such as knowledge about the organization and its processes) and external knowledge (such as knowledge about the market and industry trends). iii.
KMID shall organize a team who may help the innovators to ideate.
The team generates new ideas for innovative products, services, or business ventures.
This may involve brainstorming sessions, market research, and feedback from customers and stakeholders. b.
Screening and selection.
The KMID screens and evaluates the potential of the ideas based on criteria such as feasibility, market potential, and strategic fit.
The most promising ideas are selected for further development. c.
Concept development: The KMID and the team develop a concept for the product, service, or business venture, including features, benefits, and target markets. d.
Business planning.
The team develops a business plan for the start-up project, including financial projections, market analysis, and a marketing plan.

e.
Validation.
KMID shall assists the innovators to test and validate their ideas through research, market analysis, and customer feedback.
This helps to determine whether the idea is feasible, viable, and sustainable. f.
Resource allocation.
KMID assists in looking for resources, such as funding, personnel, and facilities, to support the development and launch of the start-up project. g.
Development.
Once the idea is validated, the project moves to the development stage.
This involves creating a prototype, building a minimum viable product (MVP), and refining the product or service based on user feedback. h.
Launch.
The launch stage involves bringing the product or service to market.
This may involve developing a marketing strategy, establishing distribution channels, and creating a launch plan i.
Growth.
After the product or service is launched, the focus shifts to growth and scaling.
This involves increasing market share, expanding into new markets, and attracting new customers. j.
Sustainability.
The final stage of the process involves ensuring the long-term sustainability of the start-up project.
This may involve developing a sustainable business model, establishing partnerships, and creating a strong brand identity.
